bib.title: StructGPT: A General Framework for Large Language Model to Reason over Structured Data
bib.venue: preprint (arXiv v2, 23 Oct 2023; the text prints no venue)

read.skipped: Reference list skimmed only for lineage.

question: How can a frozen LLM reason over structured data (knowledge graphs, tables, databases) in one unified way, without fine-tuning and without fitting all records in the prompt?
hypothesis: Giving the LLM specialised read interfaces to the structured data, and iterating an invoking-linearization-generation loop, lets it concentrate on reasoning and improves zero-shot and few-shot performance over feeding it the data directly.
contributions: An Iterative Reading-then-Reasoning (IRR) framework, StructGPT, with an invoking-linearization-generation procedure.
Specialised read interfaces for KG (2), table (3) and database (2).
Experiments on 8 datasets across KGQA, TableQA and Text-to-SQL, with error analysis.

method.summary: A frozen LLM (text-davinci-003 or gpt-3.5-turbo, June versions) is wrapped in a loop. At each step an interface reads a small slice of the structured data, the slice is linearized to text, and the LLM either selects useful items (relations, columns, rows, tables) or generates the answer or SQL. No parameters are trained.

other.note: numbers copied from earlier papers, not rerun

inference.prompting: Two prompt patterns, rewritten per dataset: selection ('Here are [Y]. Which [X] are most relevant to answer the question [Q]') and generation ('Based on [Y], please generate [Z] for the question [Q]'). Few-shot uses 15 exemplars for WebQSP and 32 for MetaQA, TableQA and Text-to-SQL. Zero-shot baselines use the same instruction prompt with no KG (KGQA) or with the whole table or DB schema (TableQA, Text-to-SQL), with no special treatment of over-length input.
inference.retrieval: Interfaces: KG Extract_Neighbor_Relations(e), Extract_Triples(e,{r}); Table Extract_Column_Name(T), Extract_Columns(T,{c}), Extract_SubTable(T,{c},{j}); DB Extract_Table&Column_Name(D), Extract_Tables_Information({T}). KGQA runs two sequential invocations per hop, multi-hop adds an LLM sufficiency check before continuing; TableQA runs three; Text-to-SQL runs two.

parameters.kg_linearization: relations and triples concatenated into one sentence with separation and boundary symbols
parameters.table_linearization: cells converted to triples then row-wise, e.g. 'row 1: (year, 1896), (city, Athens)', rows joined by a separator

other.manual_check: For KGQA, a manual double-check judges whether wrong answers are included when the LLM returns several answers (following Tan et al., 2023).

metrics.name: Hits@1
metrics.definition: whether the top-1 predicted answer is correct (KGQA), with a manual check for multiple answers

metrics.name: Denotation accuracy
metrics.definition: set-level equivalence of predicted and gold answer (WTQ, WikiSQL)

metrics.name: Execution accuracy (EX)
metrics.definition: whether the execution results of predicted and gold SQL are the same (Spider variants)

limits: Authors concede: only two instruction-following LLMs (ChatGPT, Davinci-003) are used; weaker instruction followers are untested.
Authors concede: only QA over structured data is evaluated, not data-to-text or formal-language-to-text.
Authors concede: answer-format control is hard and format errors remain.
Topic entity must already be linked to the KG; linking is outside the method.
Closed, versioned models: the June to August ChatGPT update changed baselines by several points (Appendix A).
Single runs; no variance, seeds, decoding parameters, max iterations, token or cost figures are reported.
Supervised baseline numbers are copied from other papers, and the KGQA metric includes a manual double-check.
Zero-shot IRR hurt Davinci-003 on TabFact (80.7 to 76.5), against the text's claim of consistent gains.
Evaluated KGQA only up to 3 hops on MetaQA and 2 on WebQSP; no large-scale latency or cost comparison.

terms.definition: construct specialized interfaces to collect relevant evidence from structured data (reading), and let LLMs concentrate on the reasoning task based on the collected information (reasoning)
invoke an interface to extract evidence, linearize it into a textual prompt, and feed the prompt into the LLM for generation (selecting useful data or predicting the answer)
